programmes.t: Cold War: The Tech Race S1 - "Golden Age of Science"
programmes.d: Military funding drives a boom in earth sciences and biological research, creating advanced weapons alongside deeper insights into our world.

programmes.t: Cold War: The Tech Race S1 - "Information Is Power"
programmes.d: Cold War secrecy accelerates spy tech, satellite surveillance, and early computer networks, laying the foundation for modern global communications.

programmes.t: Cold War: The Tech Race S1 - "Race to Space"
programmes.d: Superpower rivalries turn missile tech toward orbital supremacy, driving historic milestones from early satellite launches to landing on the moon.
Artillery, the King of Battle, is explored as gunners train with powerful weapons and prepare for modern combat deployment.

programmes.t: Combat Forces S1 - "First Ten Combat Missions"
programmes.d: During the Vietnam War, the USAF learned most pilot losses happened in their first 10 missions, leading to intense training that saves lives.
At Fort Benning’s Army Combatives School, soldiers train in brutal hand-to-hand combat, learning real-world skills to fight and survive.
Stealthy diesel submarines challenge nuclear subs. Inside a NATO exercise, we explore why they’re so deadly in the Norwegian fjords.
Tank crews train for deployment, mastering modern armored warfare where heavy tanks protect soldiers and dominate the battlefield.
Silent and deadly, snipers train in elite schools, mastering long‑range weapons, stealth, and fieldcraft to become the battlefield’s ultimate asset.
Urban combat is brutal and unforgiving. At training sites worldwide, soldiers learn the tactics and teamwork needed to survive deadly city battles.
New pilots train in air‑to‑air combat at an international exercise, mastering dogfighting and modern fighter jet technology.
Airborne troops train as force multipliers, learning how paratroopers drop behind enemy lines to seize targets and launch ambushes.
Combat medics risk it all to save soldiers under fire. We join their training to see what it takes to save lives in the field.
Basic training transforms civilians into soldiers, sailors, and airmen through intense physical and psychological tests.
Combat fitness builds soldiers’ strength, endurance, and resilience, teaching skills crucial for survival, sometimes adapted for civilians.
The untold secret story of war production that shaped the WWII, beginning with how the German aviation industry came to dominate the skies of Europe.
The story behind the Krupp company, who were responsible for the manufacture of two of Germany's most feared war products - the Panzer Tank and the U-boat.
The role played by engineering giant Vickers during the WWII, including the development of the Spitfire.
How the Americans out-produced the rest of the world so quickly and by such a huge margin, including the likes of General Motors.
Henry Ford's plan to build a giant factory in Michigan, covering 3.5million sq ft and including an aircraft production line half a mile in length.
The sabotaging efforts of Peugeot in Nazi-occupied France, where the bosses and workers cooperated with the Resistance to hinder the Nazis' use of military vehicles.
The story of America's `Liberty Ships', which were produced in incredible numbers and became known as the Model T Fords of the ocean.
The remarkable story of how Stalin's massive war factories were dismantled and moved east on one and half million railway trucks, to avoid being lost to the Nazis.

programmes.t: Race of Life S1 - "Survival of the Fittest"
programmes.d: Animals adapt for survival. Crocodiles, ancient and resilient, boast slow metabolism and efficient physiology. Sharks retain successful traits over time. Whales, from land to sea, evolve with echolocation and robust anatomy, ensuring survival.

programmes.t: Race of Life S1 - "The Big Cats"
programmes.d: Cheetahs race towards endangerment.Leopards thrive as opportunistic hunters.Lions reign atop the food chain. Snow leopards navigate treacherous terrain.Tigers persevere. Each big cat surviving maturity claims victory in life's relentless race.

programmes.t: Race of Life S1 - "The Great Desert Race"
programmes.d: Deserts, harsh and arid, challenge life with scant rainfall. Desert animals adapt to conserve water, relying on food for hydration. They seek shade, burrow, or became nocturnal to survive extreme temperatures.

Elephants, thrive on vegetation, though they're not averse to confrontation. Rhinos, resilient yet endangered, face threats from predators and humanity. Hippos, formidable and protective, safeguard their young from crocodiles and other predators.
